reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes film breakdown, rust transition to hydroxyl iron oxides, and a secondary protective layer at room temperature, but it does not address high-temperature behavior, N/F-rich film composition, or the effect of varying passivation quality, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Passivation film on Q235 is rich in N and F and acts as an initial electrochemical barrier
Chloride ingress causes film breakdown, transitioning from passivation to mixed rust (hydroxyl iron oxides)
At room temperature, a secondary self-limiting protective rust layer forms after film breakdown
At high temperature, film breakdown is accelerated, leading to a discontinuous/brittle rust layer with altered kinetics and hardness
